title: Viva Engage: sensitivity labels for communities (Microsoft Purview)
summary: Hold: the licensing paragraph omits Microsoft's requirement to assign a Standard/Plan 1 licence alongside a Premium/Plan 2 licence for sensitivity labelling. The roadmap facts and printed commands check out; the portal paths stop early on the correct pages, and the checklist's default-label decision has no corresponding control row.

claims.claim: The roadmap says organisations can now manually apply Information Protection sensitivity labels in Engage.
claims.quote: Your organization can now manually apply Information Protection sensitivity labels in Engage.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes administrators creating labels and publishing policies to determine who can manually label Engage content.
claims.quote: Sensitivity label support in this new application will allow admins to create labels and configure label publishing policies to determine which users and groups can manually label content in Engage.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes end users labelling communities to classify and protect data through privacy and external user access controls.
claims.quote: End users will be able to manually apply labels to Engage communities and in turn classify and protect their sensitive data via privacy and external user access controls.

claims.claim: Purview labels configured with associated policies can be applied to Viva Engage communities.
claims.quote: After you configure sensitivity labels with their associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, these labels can be applied to communities in your organization.

claims.claim: An administrator can select an Engage default label in Purview label policy settings.
claims.quote: As an example, select a preferred default label for Engage communities in Microsoft Purview as part of label policy settings.

claims.claim: The Engage default takes precedence over the default label for sites.
claims.quote: This new default takes precedence over the default label for sites.

claims.claim: Engage communities can have a more permissive default than SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Create a more permissive default for Engage communities, while maintaining a more restrictive default for sites.

claims.fix: The path is correct but stops on the labels page. For classic labels extend it to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > + Create a label > Define the scope for this label > Groups & sites > Define protection settings for groups and sites > Privacy and external user access settings > Privacy and external user access'.
